title: What the wink switches are, now that they sit on the lit plate
ask: Which switch should the two winks be on the plate left of the wheel: the 16 mm metal buttons in the cart moved apart, a changeover pushbutton under a lit key cap like the plate's other keys, or 12 mm panel buttons?
why: Your sketch puts the two winks 19 mm apart with a lit wink face on each (ideas I-002, I-006), and the plate's board is now drawn to it (Y21). The buttons in the cart for the winks (P083: DMWD metal pushbuttons, 16 mm thread, size confirm) have bezels about 19 mm across, so at that pitch they touch and leave 2.5 mm of board between their holes, and a metal button cannot be lit through: the wink face would have to be a lit window above each button, not the button itself. A wink switch has to be a changeover - one contact that opens while the other closes - because a held wink opens the other lamp's relay return (D-189, D-482); an ordinary key switch has one contact and will not do. Nothing is bought yet, so this costs nothing to change now and a re-drawn plate later.
options:
(a) Keep the P083 buttons. Move the two winks apart on the plate (about 18 and 46 mm from its edge, so the plate's face changes a little) and light a wink face through a window above each button. Nothing new to buy; the plate board and the sketch move.
(b) A changeover pushbutton under a lit key cap, like the plate's other keys. A board-mount SPDT momentary pushbutton (C&K 8125 class, about $4 each, two) on the plate board, the wink face lit through its cap from the plate's own light driver, exactly as the sketch draws it. The three wink wires then end on a header on the plate board and their two resistors move onto it. P083 ($12, in the cart, unpaid) is dropped; the plate board is redrawn for it (my time, not yours).
(c) 12 mm panel-mount changeover buttons (one normally open and one normally closed contact), about $8 each. They fit the sketch's spacing; the lit face still needs a window above each unless a lit-cap one can be found, which is a rare part and a parts round to look for.
recommend: (b), unless you want the feel of a metal button under your finger - then (a)
stops: The plate board's wink holes and the plate's face (Y21, luxury LP20's sibling plate); P083 and P199; DV24's terminals (where the wink wires end); the plate board's place in the bench order (Y18).
